events.statement: The operational machine was used for wartime Lorenz cryptanalysis.
events.uncertainty: The exact operational start date, later adoption by other organizations and commercialization are not asserted.

events.statement: The program service became formal in 1950, with operators to run programs.
events.uncertainty: The precise start day and size of the service community are not specified. The date of the queueing system is not established by the cited chronology.

events.statement: LEO I ran a bakery costing job for its company.
events.uncertainty: Later full business dependence began separately; do not claim the computer was offered to outside buyers in 1951.

events.statement: IBM released FORTRAN commercially in 1957.
events.uncertainty: Source gives year only; number of users, price and first installation are not established.

events.statement: WorldWideWeb files were made available by FTP and announced to alt.hypertext.
events.uncertainty: Internet access was unequal; this does not imply universal awareness or immediate mass adoption.

events.label: 28 May 1822
events.statement: Forbes examined a patient with a stethoscope in his Chichester Dispensary practice on 28 May 1822.
events.uncertainty: This is one practitioner’s use, not the first British use or general adoption.

events.statement: A publication described monaural stethoscope in forbes’s practice.
events.uncertainty: Publication of a report is not proof of first invention, deployment, community acceptance or sale.

events.statement: Marshall used a carbolic antiseptic method in a Preston clinical case.
events.uncertainty: This case does not establish general acceptance, efficacy compared with alternatives, or the first carbolic use.

events.statement: A publication described carbolic antiseptic wound treatment.
events.uncertainty: Publication of a report is not proof of first invention, deployment, community acceptance or sale.

events.statement: National Technical Laboratories sold Beckman acidimeters during 1935.
events.uncertainty: The source does not establish the first transaction, exact month or later model designations.

events.statement: The Oxford team administered penicillin in a hospital clinical trial.
events.uncertainty: The account is a later institutional history. Supplies were limited and the patient died; no worldwide first or general access is claimed.

events.label: by 1979-1
events.statement: A Genentech-led team used recombinant bacterial plasmids to produce human insulin chains for biochemical research.
events.uncertainty: This was laboratory expression, not sale of Humulin; later industrial processes were modified.

events.statement: A publication described bacterial plasmid cloning for insulin research.
events.uncertainty: Publication of a report is not proof of first invention, deployment, community acceptance or sale.

events.label: by 1979-5
events.statement: Researchers applied chemical sequencing to determine the adenovirus 2 EcoRI-F sequence.
events.uncertainty: The paper gives a use-by bound, not first uptake; later decline is not dated here.

events.statement: A publication described chemical cleavage dna sequencing.
events.uncertainty: Publication of a report is not proof of first invention, deployment, community acceptance or sale.

events.label: by 1980-9
events.statement: Kung and Goldstein reported using seven hybridoma-derived monoclonal antibodies for T-cell analysis.
events.uncertainty: This covers the reported clones and study, not all diagnostic or therapeutic antibodies.

events.statement: A publication described hybridoma antibodies for human t-cell analysis.
events.uncertainty: Publication of a report is not proof of first invention, deployment, community acceptance or sale.

events.label: By 1982
events.statement: Lilly retrospectively reports a Humulin launch in 1982; a historical account reports Humulin R and N reached the U.S. market that year.
events.uncertainty: Lilly’s CEO reports a 1982 launch without specifying geography; Health Action International dates U.S. market introduction to 1982, while a National Academies account says first sold in 1983. The discrepancy is unresolved; these retrospective accounts do not establish a precise first-availability day or every patient’s access.

events.label: by 1989-10
events.statement: A 1989 immunology review reports Taq-based PCR used across several immunological research applications.
events.uncertainty: The review does not establish first use, the fraction of all laboratories, or first commercial availability.

events.statement: A publication described taq-based pcr in immunology.
events.uncertainty: Publication of a report is not proof of first invention, deployment, community acceptance or sale.

events.label: by 2015-11-25
events.statement: A Toronto-led research team applied CRISPR–Cas9 screens to five human cell lines.
events.uncertainty: This event concerns the specific 2015 Hart study and does not establish first use of CRISPR–Cas9 editing or screening in human cells.

events.statement: A publication described crispr–cas9 human-cell fitness screens.
events.uncertainty: This event concerns the specific 2015 Hart study and does not establish first use of CRISPR–Cas9 editing or screening in human cells.

events.statement: Collaborating teams used portable nanopore sequencing for outbreak surveillance in Guinea.
events.uncertainty: This is a specific 2015 deployment; it does not establish that all outbreaks used it or prove earliest nanopore commercialization.

events.statement: A publication described portable nanopore ebola surveillance.
events.uncertainty: Publication of a report is not proof of first invention, deployment, community acceptance or sale.
